groups.passage: Some species of ants keep slaves. Probably the best known for the practice is the large brownish-red Amazon ant. A slave raid starts with an assembly of the Amazon warriors outside their own nest. Then, almost [[26]] at a given signal, the group begins to march toward the colony [[27]]. When the Amazons reach the nest of their intended victims, a fierce battle may take place. The Amazons fight on [[28]] they seize the pupae of the raided nest. They carry these back home. In time the pupae develop into adults and spend their lives working for the Amazons. sections.title: 四、文意選填(10%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第31至40題，每題一個空格，請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其英文字母代號標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage:
The term “standard of living” usually refers to the economic well-being enjoyed by a person, family, community, or nation. A standard of living is considered high when it includes [[31]] necessities but also certain comforts and luxuries; it is considered low when food, clean water, housing, and [[32]] necessities are limited or lacking.
Different [[33]] have been employed by economists to measure standard of living. One of [[34]] measures is to calculate the percentage of income that people spend on certain necessities. The higher this percentage is, the [[35]] is the standard of living of these people.
The U.S. has one of the world’s highest standards of living. But income is not distributed [[36]] throughout its population. Some Americans enjoy great wealth, [[37]] others suffer in extreme poverty. Americans [[38]] different racial and educational backgrounds may vary in their standards of living. People living in different parts of the U.S. [[39]] show different standards of living. Of course, in determining overall standards of living of Americans, factors [[40]] household composition and family size need also to be taken into consideration.

sections.title: 五、閱讀測驗(30%)
sections.instructions: 說明︰第41至55題，每題請分別根據各篇文章之文意選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得2分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage:
Laura was at the door, thrusting a bracelet at Amy. It was a thin gold chain with a heart dangling on it and Amy loved it the minute she saw it. Amy gave Laura a big hug and promised that she would come back to see her. But she really didn’t know if she would ever come back to the little town. She watched as Laura walked down the block, turning and waving and walking backwards until she got to the corner.
Mama was hurrying her. Amy made sure her gold bracelet was secure on her wrist. Then she put on both her sweater and her coat so that she wouldn’t have to carry them. They could take only what they could carry, and her two suitcases were already full.
Mama took a last look around the house, going from room to room. Amy followed her, trying to recall how each one had looked when they were filled with furniture and rugs and pictures and books. They went out for a last look at the garden Papa loved. If he were here now, Amy knew he would pick one of the prettiest carnations and gave it to Mama. She would beam and put it in her best crystal vase. But now the garden looked shabby and bare. It looked the way Amy felt--lonely and abandoned.

options.D: Amy and her mother carried only a few suitcases with them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true according to the passage?

options.B: Amy turned and walked backwards as she left.
options.C: Amy’s father was not around when they were leaving.
options.D: Amy did not know if she could keep her promise to Laura.

groups.passage:
In the last several decades, the western world has been rediscovering the soybean, a plant whose use dates before recorded history in Asia. For thousands of years, the Chinese have valued highly the soybean, considering it one of the five important grains (along with rice, millet, barley, and wheat). Since it is cheap to produce and rich in protein, and has many uses, the soybean could provide food to the world’s growing population. Besides, soybeans can be fed to a variety of other animals ranging from livestock to silk worms.
The soybean is an almost perfect source of protein. If you are a vegetarian, or if your diet includes little meat, soy protein is a good alternative, and may even be essential to maintaining your health. The soybean’s high fiber content is beneficial in preventing digestive disorders. The soybean is free of cholesterol, and more importantly, the soy oil contains some special substances, called Omega 3 fatty acids, which reduce cholesterol and prevent blood from clotting in human body. Research shows that consuming a minimum of 25 grams of soy protein a day can lower blood cholesterol levels in people with high cholesterol problems.
In view of all these strengths, in the 1930s the United States and Canada undertook a research project in which they managed to breed an especially nutritious soybean with a high oil content. Since then, the United States has become the world’s largest producer of soybeans and has exported much of its soybean produce. In recent years, the soybean has been used in making many different foods and has become the atom of health food. Health-conscious Americans are adding tofu, the most popular soybean product, to salads and using it as a meat substitute. In the health food stores of major cities, it is now possible to buy tofu burgers and even tofu hot dogs.

options.B: Health-conscious Americans are using more tofu in their diet.
options.C: The soybean provides food for the world’s growing population.
options.D: The soybean is healthful and has become popular in the western world.

groups.passage:
Big brothers and sisters usually develop leadership tendencies early in life, mainly because of the responsibilities for younger children given to them by their parents. Firstborns, under normal circumstances, are usually the most strongly motivated toward achievement. This is mainly a result of parental expectations. Research also suggests that firstborn children generally become more conservative than other children because they receive most of the parental discipline. Used to caring for others, they are more likely to move toward such leadership professions as teaching and politics. Less social and flexible because they become accustomed in the very early years to acting alone, they may have difficulty making close friends.
By contrast, later children are more likely to be more relaxed and sociable because their parents are more relaxed. However, later children are often less ambitious and may be uncomfortable making decisions for others. This may help explain why younger children tend to favor the creative fields such as music, art, and writing. Later children may make good salespersons because persuasion may have been the only tool they had to deal with older siblings. Younger children tend to remain forever “the baby,” enjoyable to be around, but at times overdependent on others.

groups.passage:
According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), medical waste is a major source of dioxin pollution in the country. Linked to the dioxin issue is the use of PVC plastic, which is widely used in the production of blood bags, plastic tubing, and other products in hospitals and health clinics. Dioxin is an unwanted byproduct that is created when PVC is burned. Dioxin travels by air currents and settles onto grass, which is then eaten by cows and chickens in their feed. We eat polluted dairy products and meat and take the dioxin into our bodies, where it is stored in our fat for years and builds up over time. In this way, dioxin is globally distributed, and as a consequence, every member of the human population is constantly exposed to this poisonous substance. This poses special problems for childbearing women, who pass dioxin to an unborn baby or to a breastfeeding baby. In fact, the infant is the most vulnerable member of society to this chemical.
Plastics used to account for as little as 10% of medical waste in the late 1970s, before disposables began rapidly replacing reusables. They now make up as much as 30%. The EPA estimates that the average levels of dioxin in all Americans are so high that we can expect to see a variety of health effects, including cancer. Given the harm caused by the burning of medical waste, physicians and nurses have the responsibility to take a lead in reducing the use of plastics in the hospitals. After all, they can’t be treating cancer on the inside of hospitals and contributing to it on the outside.

questions.stem: What is the major message the author is trying to convey to readers?

options.A: All people, especially those working in the hospitals, should reduce the use of plastics.
options.B: Americans should lead the world to fight dioxin pollution, or mankind will die out soon.
options.C: We had better eat more vegetables than meat in order to reduce the risk of dioxin pollution.
options.D: We had better not breastfeed our babies, since babies are most likely to be poisoned by dioxin.

questions.stem: Dioxin is produced __________.

options.B: in the making of hospital blood bags
options.D: in the handling of all kinds of medical waste

questions.stem: What does it in the last line refer to?
Which of the following statements can be inferred from the article?

options.B: Dioxin can be released from our bodies, if we drink a lot of clean, pure water.
options.C: Using reusables as people did in the old days will help lessen dioxin pollution.
options.D: You have to lose weight, or the amount of dioxin in your body fat will kill you.

tags.topic: dioxin pollution from burning plastic medical waste

sections.title: 一、簡答題(10%)
sections.instructions:
說明︰1.閱讀下面這篇文章，然後簡答下列問題。答案必須寫在「答案卷」上。
2.請依序作答，並標明題號。答案應簡明扼要，只寫重要詞彙(key words)，請勿超過五個英文單詞(words)。每題2分，共10分。注意：請勿抄下整句或整行，否則不予計分。

groups.passage:
It’s easier for the human face to smile than frown. It takes twice as many muscles to frown as it does to smile. Moreover, we do not have to “learn” to do it. Although babies imitate the facial expressions they see, smiling isn’t just learned by imitation. Children born blind never see anybody smile, but they show the same kinds of smiles under the same situations as sighted people.
Smiling is of great help to us. Some studies suggest that the act of shaping our mouths into a smile (creating a “physical smile”) can help us see the brighter, funnier side of things. People wearing the physical smile tend to feel happier. In addition, smiles signal to others that we are people who might be nice to talk to and work with—and that can help us make friends.
Unfortunately, sometimes you may find it difficult to smile. Anything from getting a bad grade on a test to losing an important game can make you feel sad. In such hard times, there seems to be no reason to smile. But there is some good part to almost every bad thing. Turning something that seems all bad into something good is one way to help you smile. Hanging around people who are positive and in good moods is another way to help you find your smile again.

sections.title: 二、英文作文(20%)
sections.instructions:
說明︰1.依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2.文長120個單詞(words)左右。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem: 提示︰請以自己的經驗為例，敘述當你感到不快樂或情緒低落時，(除了簡答題選文中所提及的方法外，)你最常用哪一種方法幫自己渡過低潮，並舉實例說明這個方法何以有效。

tags.topic: the method you use most often to get through unhappy or low moods (other than those in the short-answer passage), with a real example of why it works
coping with unhappiness and low moods

extraction.method: Word 版（paper-4.doc → soffice 轉 docx → python-docx）為主要文字來源（含 run 格式檢查粗體／底線），與 pdftotext -layout 題本（paper-3.pdf）以程式逐詞比對；vocabulary 與閱讀題幹的空格底線長度取自 pdftotext；Read 看題本 PDF 全部 8 頁影像確認版面、粗體、題組與句子配合題表格；答案取自 answer-2.pdf 第 2 頁英文考科（五科合併檔，pdftotext＋頁面影像核對）；人工校對。
issues: 結構核對：gsat-spec.json 的 legacy_gsat 僅依正式考試核對（scope_note 註明不含補考），本卷結構與「91–92」期別完全一致——詞彙與慣用語 1–15（15分）、句子配合題 16–20（5分，右欄選項 A–J）、綜合測驗 21–30（10分，2篇×5空格）、文意選填 31–40（10分，選項 A–J）、閱讀測驗 41–55（4篇 3+4+4+4 題，每題2分，30分）、簡答題 5題×2分（10分，只寫重要詞彙、不超過五個英文單詞）、英文作文 20分（文長「120個單詞(words)左右」，與 essay_length_by_year「91-94,96-98」相符）；合計 100 分。題本封面印「考試時間：100 分鐘」「第壹部份 ˙單一選擇題共55 題」「第貳部份 ˙非選擇題共2大題」「選擇題答錯不倒扣」，time_minutes 填 100。題本部分名稱原文為「第壹部份：單一選擇題」「第貳部份：非選擇題」（「部份」），part 欄比照 gsat-92 填「單一選擇題」「非選擇題」。

評分原則與統計：units.json 中本卷只有 paper／paper_word／answer，沒有 scoring 與 stats。簡答題 1–5 的 answer／accepted_answers／scoring_notes 一律填 null（官方未公布參考答案，未自行作答）；作文 answer、scoring_notes 亦為 null。data/raw/ceec/gsat/92/ 中的 stats-1.xls、stats-2.xls 屬於 92 學年度正式考試（報考人數 164,521；stats-2 英文工作表標星號的 55 題答案 CABDB… 與 gsat-92 正式考答案完全相同，與本卷答案 BACAC… 不符），不可用於補考，全部小題 stats 填 null。validator 的「整份考卷沒有任何統計資料」warning 由此而來，屬合理（大考中心未公布補考統計）。
非選擇題題號：簡答題題本印為 1.–5.，與選擇題第1–5題重號；比照 gsat-92 慣例，no 保留 1–5、label 改為「簡答1」–「簡答5」；英文作文題本未編號，no 填 1、label 為「作文」。validator 的「題號重複 [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]」warning 由此而來，屬合理。

答案：answer-2.pdf 為「九十二學年度學科能力測驗（補考）」國文、英文、數學、社會、自然五科合併答案表，只取第 2 頁英文考科 1–55 題；pdftotext 與頁面影像一致，並逐題與題意核對無矛盾（例如 16 J whose car was stolen、17 G should John be allowed…、40 I such as）。answer-1.pdf、paper-1.pdf、paper-2.doc 為正式考試檔案，未使用。

文字來源比對：Word 版與 pdftotext 題本以程式逐詞比對，英文內容（選文、題幹、選項、句子配合題左右欄）完全一致，差異只有版面（句子配合題兩欄排列、文意選填題號）；並以頁面影像確認。說明文字的冒號照原文保留：一、二、三、五大題、簡答題、作文說明與「提示︰」為 U+FE30「︰」，文意選填說明與簡答題「注意：」為全形「：」。title 的「（補考）」比照 ast-109-makeup 用全形括號（題本封面為半形「(補考)」）。

空白與格式正規化：排版造成的 Tab、連續空白與手動換行壓成單一空白，Word 版說明文字的手動斷行（句子配合題、簡答題）接回，只在 1.／2. 項目之間保留換行；各題組前「41-43 為題組」等標示為版面標題，未放入 passage。詞彙題空格依 PDF 底線長度照錄（第5題為 5 個底線、其餘 6 個；第2題「a(n)______」、第11題「______--」、第12題「______.」與前後文字之間無空格，照 PDF）；閱讀題幹空格為 10 個底線。克漏字空格原文寫法不一（21–25、31–40 為「__(21)__」，26–30 為「___(26)___」「____(27)____」），一律轉為 [[題號]]。第6題選項原文「(A)furiously」代號後無空格、句子配合題與文意選填選項 I、J 原文排為「( I )」「( J )」，皆不影響選項內容。句子配合題右欄選項原文沒有開頭省略號，照錄。

粗體：第43題題幹的 NOT、第54題題幹與 52–55 選文末句「contributing to it on the outside」中的 it、簡答題選文第3段的 hard times、作文提示的「一種」在題本為粗體（非底線），依 schema 不保留格式、未加 <u>。第54題「What does it in the last line refer to?」所指即選文最後一句的 it（contributing to it on the outside），顯示給學生時可能需要另行標示。

照原文保留的原文錯誤或怪異處（PDF 與 Word 版皆同）：21–25 選文「roasted chicken, chili, turkey loaf, turkey loaf, meatballs」turkey loaf 重複、「you [[25]] with you classmates」（應為 your）、「recipe handouts and , more importantly」逗號前多一空格；41–43 選文「he would pick one of the prettiest carnations and gave it to Mama」（依文法應為 give）、「It looked the way Amy felt--lonely and abandoned.」以兩個連字號表示破折號；44–47 選文「has become the atom of health food」用字語意不通（原文如此，未更動）；簡答題選文「work with—and」為 em dash。
